tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_logs
entries.description: A run's log lines, in time order, each with its time on the run's clock and its stream. Streams: stdout and stderr (your agent system), setup (the platform: install, the free models' warm-up), input (what the browsers received; run_inputs reads them better, so they're left out unless you ask). Narrow with from/to (e.g. from 02:10 to 02:40), grep, browser; tail for the last lines; page with after. About 30 tokens a line.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

stream.description: Only these streams, comma-separated: stdout, stderr, setup, input; "all" is every one. Default: stdout, stderr and setup.

grep.description: Only lines containing this text, case-insensitive; a|b matches either

browser.description: Only the platform's lines about this browser (its inputs, a browser it stopped)

tail.description: Only the last n matching lines

after.description: Continue after a previous page: its `next` value

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_profile
entries.description: Where a run's time went, bucket by bucket (30 s, 1 min or 5 min): per browser, its inputs and how long its screen was changing (– idle); model calls, seconds in calls and cost. Then the critical path: the longest stretches with nothing happening, the slowest calls, and when each browser went quiet. About 1.5–3k tokens.

bucket.description: Bucket size (default: by the run's length)

"""Quick decisions with the hosted Clef model: cheap, fast, calibrated. Use it for the many small judgements
(what kind of page is this, which of these links, is this the right document) and keep Qwen for reading and
reasoning. Each call still adds its simulated cost, but at a fraction of a chat call.

Division of work in the swarm: Clef answers closed questions (pick one of N, yes/no) - the popup guard's "what is this
overlay and which button closes it", the site-role mapping, the receipt sanity check. Qwen does everything that has to
produce text or values: browsing steps, extraction, the brief, follow-up planning, gate field values, image
transcription. Every Clef caller falls back to Qwen (or to a safe default) when Clef is missing, slow or unsure.

    kind, p = await decide.choose({"page": text}, "What is this page?", PAGE_KINDS)
    p_yes   = await decide.yes({"mail": subject}, "Is this mail about tender REF exactly?")

The API (POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide) takes a `state` (text or JSON), up to 4 images as base64 data URLs and
named questions: "choice" (criteria: {option: description}), "noul" (probability of yes) and "score"
(criteria: a list of 2-10 levels, lowest first). Set "clef" in agent.json "models" so a run waits for it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import logging
import os

import httpx

from swarm import timeline
from swarm.bidmath import plain

log = logging.getLogger("decide")

MAX_IMAGES = 4
_sem = asyncio.Semaphore(12)        # the team may run 16 Clef calls at once, across all its runs
usage = {"calls": 0, "input_tokens": 0}
_transport = None                   # tests swap in an httpx.MockTransport

# what a page can be, for agents that need to know where they are before acting
PAGE_KINDS = {
    "login": "a sign-in form asking for username and password",
    "consent": "a cookie or consent wall that must be accepted before the content",
    "error": "an error or 'service unavailable' page that offers a retry",
    "locked": "content blocked behind a robot check, slider or other unlock step",
    "list": "a list, table or search results to pick an entry from",
    "document": "a document, record, message or form with the actual content",
    "other": "anything else",
}


class ClefError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def available() -> bool:
    """Is Clef hosted for this run? (Local runs without it go straight to the Qwen path.)"""
    return bool(os.environ.get("CLEF_BASE_URL") and os.environ.get("CLEF_API_KEY"))


def picked(answer: dict | None) -> tuple[str | None, float]:
    """(choice, confidence) of one "choice" answer; (None, 0) when it is missing."""
    if not isinstance(answer, dict) or not answer.get("choice"):
        return None, 0.0
    choice = answer["choice"]
    return choice, float(answer.get("confidence", (answer.get("probabilities") or {}).get(choice, 0)) or 0)


def data_url(png: bytes, mime: str = "image/png") -> str:
    return f"data:{mime};base64,{base64.b64encode(png).decode()}"


async def decide(state, questions: dict, images: list[bytes] | None = None, retries: int = 2) -> dict:
    """One Clef call with several named questions; returns the `answers` object."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": questions}
    if images:
        body["images"] = [data_url(i) if isinstance(i, (bytes, bytearray)) else i for i in images[:MAX_IMAGES]]
    url = os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"}
    last = None
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        try:
            async with _sem, httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=180, transport=_transport) as client:
                started = timeline.now()
                response = await client.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
                timeline.add("model.call", "clef", started)
            if response.status_code == 400:      # our question is malformed: retrying will not help
                raise ClefError(response.text[:300])
            response.raise_for_status()
            reply = response.json()
            usage["calls"] += 1
            usage["input_tokens"] += (reply.get("usage") or {}).get("input_tokens", 0)
            return reply["answers"]
        except ClefError:
            raise
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - timeouts, 5xx, a model waking up
            last = error
            await asyncio.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise ClefError(f"Clef unavailable: {type(last).__name__}: {last}")


async def choose(state, instructions: str, options: dict[str, str],
                 images: list[bytes] | None = None) -> tuple[str, float]:
    """Pick one of `options` ({key: description}); returns (key, confidence)."""
    answers = await decide(state, {"q": {"type": "choice", "instructions": instructions, "criteria": options}},
                           images)
    return picked(answers["q"])


async def yes(state, question: str, images: list[bytes] | None = None) -> float:
    """Probability (0-1) that the answer to a yes/no question about `state` is yes."""
    answers = await decide(state, {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}, images)
    return float(answers["q"]["noul"])


async def score(state, instructions: str, levels: list[str], images: list[bytes] | None = None) -> float:
    """A rating on `levels` (lowest first), as a float index into them."""
    answers = await decide(state, {"q": {"type": "score", "instructions": instructions, "criteria": levels}},
                           images)
    return float(answers["q"]["score"])


async def page_kind(page, with_screenshot: bool = False, chars: int = 2500) -> tuple[str, float]:
    """What kind of page a Playwright page shows (see PAGE_KINDS), from its text and optionally a screenshot."""
    text = plain(await page.evaluate("() => (document.querySelector('main') || document.body).innerText"))[:chars]
    shots = [await page.screenshot(type="jpeg", quality=60)] if with_screenshot else None
    state = {"url": page.url, "title": plain(await page.title()), "text": text}
    return await choose(state, "What kind of page is the browser showing?", PAGE_KINDS,
                        [data_url(s, "image/jpeg") for s in shots] if shots else None)

(`use_vision=False`): capturing them hung in the sandbox browsers, and `read_page` already reads canvas labels and
    hidden text. `flash`: short replies + compact prompt (see module doc). `stop_reserve`: stop when the run has this
    many seconds left (default: the SUBMIT reserve). `extra_tools(tools)` may register more actions. Pages read with a
    `topic` reach `on_record` as {"kind": "page", "data": {...}}.
    A PopupGuard (swarm/guard.py) clears popups, notices and error pages next to the agent; `careful=True` limits it to
    noise without inputs (the bid submitter). `dedupe_reads`: read_page of a URL another agent already saved returns
    the saved text instead of opening it again (off for mails that change, such as TANs). `idle_steps`: after the
    first saved page/fact, stop once this many steps in a row saved nothing new (the caller resumes).
    """
    records: list[dict] = []
    progress = {"saved_at": None, "idle_stop": False}     # step of the last saved page/fact

    def reserve() -> float:
        """Seconds-left mark at which this browse stops: fixed, or the live submission reserve plus `stop_extra`."""
        if stop_reserve is not None:
            return stop_reserve
        return ctx.stop_at(stop_extra) if ctx is not None and hasattr(ctx, "stop_at") else stop_extra

    async def emit(rec: dict):
        """Pass a record on; `on_record` may return a string to refuse a fact (the record action reports it)."""
        if on_record:
            refused = await on_record(rec)
            if isinstance(refused, str) and refused:
                return refused
        records.append(rec)
        progress["saved_at"] = len(step_started)
        return None

    step_started: list[float] = []
    tools = build_tools(ctx, site_id, author, emit, dedupe_reads=dedupe_reads, stop_on_record=stop_on_record)
    if extra_tools:
        extra_tools(tools)

    tab = await responsive_tab(tab or main_tab(browser))
    await tab.open()
    session = make_session(ctx, tab, vision=bool(use_vision))
    memory = CAREFUL_MEMORY if careful else "1-4 short sentences: last step ok/failed, facts to keep, next goal"
    prompt = dict(flash_mode=True, override_system_message=FLASH_SYSTEM.format(max_actions=max_actions_per_step,
                                                                                memory=memory)) if flash else {}
    tips = site_tips(ctx, site_id)
    hints = hints + ("\nTips from other agents on this site:\n- " + "\n- ".join(tips) if tips else "")
    # A tab an agent already worked in is on the site (logged in, past gates): start from its current page instead of
    # browser-use opening the site's start URL from the goal again.
    reused = tab.used and bool(browsers.cdp_urls())
    tab.used = True
    browsing_llm = make_llm(flash)
    browsing_llm._usage_ctx = ctx
    agent = Agent(task=goal + ("\n\nThis tab is already on the site: start from the current page." if reused else ""),
                  llm=browsing_llm, browser_session=session, tools=tools, use_vision=use_vision,
                  use_judge=False, generate_gif=False, max_failures=6, max_actions_per_step=max_actions_per_step,
                  llm_timeout=min(CALL_TIMEOUT_S, BROWSE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_S if flash else SUBMIT_MODEL_TIMEOUT_S) + 2,
                  step_timeout=120 if flash and not careful else SUBMIT_STEP_TIMEOUT_S, directly_open_url=not reused,
                  max_history_items=HISTORY_ITEMS if flash and not careful else None,
                  max_clickable_elements_length=DOM_CHARS,
                  REDACTED,
                  extend_system_message=SYSTEM_EXTRA + (f"\n{hints}" if hints else ""), **prompt)
    async def screenshot() -> str:
        cdp = await session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
        shot = await cdp.cdp_client.send.Page.captureScreenshot(params={"format": "png"}, session_id=cdp.session_id)
        return shot["data"]

    guard = PopupGuard(ctx, author, careful=careful, screenshot=screenshot,
                       fill=lambda pairs, then_click, item_id: fill_page(session, pairs, "", then_click, item_id))
    evaluate = lambda js, *a: _evaluate(session, js, *a)  # noqa: E731
    guard_task: asyncio.Task | None = None

    async def clear_page() -> int:
        with timeline.span("guard", "sweep"):
            try:
                return await asyncio.wait_for(guard.sweep(evaluate, settle_s=GUARD_SETTLE_S), GUARD_SWEEP_S)
            except Exception as error:
                log.debug("guard sweep failed: %s", error)
                return 0

    async def before_action(name: str) -> str | None:
        """The guard owns every block: one that appeared since the model looked is cleared and the action skipped.
        A full scan only when the page's change counter moved (or a gate is still open): most actions pay one tiny
        page call."""
        if not (await guard.changed(evaluate, "action") or guard.open_gate):
            return None
        if not await clear_page():
            return None
        timeline.count("guard.skipped_actions")
        kinds = ", ".join(sorted(set(guard.last_handled))) or "popup"
        return (f"'{name}' not executed: a {kinds} covered the page after you looked; the guard cleared it. Look at "
                "the page again and continue your plan (nothing was lost).")
    tools.before_action = before_action

    async def before_step(_agent) -> None:
        nonlocal guard_task
        if ctx.seconds_left() <= reserve():
            agent.stop()
            return
        await clear_page()          # the page the model is about to see: cleared first
        await guard.changed(evaluate, "action")     # what the model sees now is the baseline for its actions
        if guard_task is None:  # from now on also between steps (popups that appear while the model thinks)
            guard_task = asyncio.create_task(guard.loop(evaluate, busy=lambda: tools.acting))
        step_started.append(timeline.now())

    secrets = [str((s.get("credentials") or {}).get("password") or "") for s in (ctx.task.get("access") or [])] \
        if ctx is not None else []

    async def after_step(_agent) -> None:
        if step_started:
            line = "no reply" if not agent.history.history or agent.history.history[-1].model_output is None else "step"
            timeline.add("browse.step", line, step_started[-1])
            if line == "no reply":
                timeline.count("steps.no_reply")
        try:
            line = _step_line(agent)
            for secret in secrets:        # the model's memory sometimes repeats the login
                if len(secret) >= 4:
                    line = line.replace(secret, "***")
            log.info("%s step %d: %s", author, agent.state.n_steps - 1, line)
        except Exception as error:
            log.debug("step line failed: %s", error)
        if idle_steps and progress["saved_at"] is not None and len(step_started) - progress["saved_at"] >= idle_steps:
            # it saved evidence, then went on without saving anything (run_7b060fa870cea9b6: 6 min on a decoy mail)
            log.warning("%s: %d steps without new evidence; ending so the caller can continue from what is saved",
                        author, idle_steps)
            timeline.count("browse.idle_stops")
            progress["idle_stop"] = True
            agent.stop()
        if session._state_timeouts >= (2 if flash and not careful else 1):
            log.warning("%s: repeated browser-state timeouts; ending this connection so the caller can reattach", author)
            timeline.count("browse.state_timeouts")
            tab.suspect = True
            agent.stop()

    failure = ""

"""Page operations (tab or iframe)."""

	def __init__(
		self, browser_session: 'BrowserSession', target_id: str, session_id: str | None = None, llm: 'BaseChatModel | None' = None
	):
		self._browser_session = browser_session
		self._client = browser_session.cdp_client
		self._target_id = target_id
		self._session_id: str | None = session_id
		self._mouse: 'Mouse | None' = None

		self._llm = llm

	async def _ensure_session(self) -> str:
		"""Ensure we have a session ID for this target."""

    sandbox runs: the submitter failed 5 times that way). `keep` is never closed, nor another agent's active tab
    (`may_close`). Returns the closed target ids."""
    async def probe(client) -> list[str]:
        targets = (await client.send.Target.getTargets())["targetInfos"]
        pages = [t for t in targets if t.get("type") == "page" and t["targetId"] != keep
                 and may_close(t["targetId"], mine)]

        async def hung(target) -> bool:
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(TAB_PROBE_S):
                    attached = await client.send.Target.attachToTarget(
                        params={"targetId": target["targetId"], "flatten": True})

    """Run `js` (an arrow function) in the agent's current tab over browser-use's own CDP session for it.

    cdp = await browser_session.get_or_create_cdp_session()

    raw = result.get("result", {}).get("value")

async def _evaluate(browser_session: BrowserSession, js: str, *args):
    """Run `js` (an arrow function) in the agent's current tab over browser-use's own CDP session for it.
    Not `must_get_current_page().evaluate`: that builds a new Page actor per call, which attaches a NEW CDP session
    and enables Page/DOM/Runtime/Network on it without ever detaching. With the guard polling twice a second each tab
    gathered hundreds of sessions, every one receiving all network events: all browsers' state captures timed out
    and the run stalled for minutes (reh_3d86cd104c8eb1b5)."""
    cdp = await browser_session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
    expression = f"({js.strip()})({', '.join(json.dumps(a) for a in args)})"
    result = await cdp.cdp_client.send.Runtime.evaluate(
        params={"expression": expression, "returnByValue": True, "awaitPromise": True}, session_id=cdp.session_id)
    if "exceptionDetails" in result:
        raise RuntimeError(f"JavaScript evaluation failed: {result['exceptionDetails']}")
    raw = result.get("result", {}).get("value")
    if isinstance(raw, (dict, list)):
        return raw
    raw = "" if raw is None else raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)   # as Page.evaluate returned it
    try:
        return json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw[:1] in ("[", "{") else raw
    except ValueError:
        return raw


async def _drag(browser_session: BrowserSession, x0: float, x1: float, y: float) -> None:
    """A real (trusted) mouse drag from x0 to x1: some sliders ignore values set by script."""
    cdp = await browser_session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
    send = cdp.cdp_client.send.Input.dispatchMouseEvent

"""Gate ownership between the popup guard and the agents, and the standby TAN lookup (no network, no browser)."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import unittest
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
from unittest import mock

import httpx

from swarm import decide, guard
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.context import Context

SLIDER_GATE = {"id": 0, "kind": "gate", "text": "Zum Entsperren ziehen. Ich bin kein Roboter",
               "buttons": [{"i": 0, "label": "Weiter", "away": False}],
               "fields": [{"type": "range", "name": "s", "label": "Zum Entsperren ziehen"},
                          {"type": "checkbox", "name": "r", "label": "Ich bin kein Roboter"}]}
CODE_GATE = dict(SLIDER_GATE, text="Empfangsnummer eingeben",
                 fields=SLIDER_GATE["fields"] + [{"type": "text", "name": "receipt", "label": "Empfangsnummer"}])
FILL = {"id": 0, "action": "fill", "kind": "gate", "then_click": "Weiter",
        "fields": [{"field": "Zum Entsperren ziehen", "value": "max"}, {"field": "Ich bin kein Roboter", "value": "true"}]}


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, reply):
        self.reply, self.calls = reply, 0

    async def ask_json(self, system, user, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        return self.reply


class GateOwnership(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    def tearDown(self):
        guard._DECISIONS.clear()
        guard._PENDING.clear()

    def test_a_gate_fill_must_cover_every_typed_field(self):
        self.assertTrue(guard.complete_fill(FILL, SLIDER_GATE))
        self.assertFalse(guard.complete_fill(FILL, CODE_GATE))        # the receipt number is missing
        with_code = dict(FILL, fields=FILL["fields"] + [{"field": "Empfangsnummer", "value": "PRD-1"}])
        self.assertTrue(guard.complete_fill(with_code, CODE_GATE))

    async def test_code_gate_is_read_from_a_screenshot_and_passed_by_the_guard(self):
        class VisionLLM(LLM):
            async def chat(self, messages, **kwargs):
                self.calls += 1
                self.image = messages[1]["content"][1]["image_url"]["url"]
                return NS(content=json.dumps({"then_click": "Weiter", "fields": FILL["fields"] + [
                    {"field": "Empfangsnummer", "value": "PRD-7"}]}))
        llm = VisionLLM({"items": [FILL]})                         # the classifier forgot the code field
        g = guard.PopupGuard(NS(llm=llm), "a", screenshot=lambda: asyncio.sleep(0, "iVBOR"))
        filled = []

        async def fake_fill(evaluate, pairs, then_click, item_id):
            filled.append(dict(pairs))
            return "ok"
        g.fill = fake_fill

        async def evaluate(js, *args):
            return {"url": "https://erp.example/notice", "items": [CODE_GATE]}
        self.assertEqual(await g.sweep(evaluate, settle_s=2), 1)
        key = ("erp.example", guard.signature(CODE_GATE))
        self.assertEqual(guard._DECISIONS[key]["action"], "read_code")
        self.assertEqual(filled[0]["Empfangsnummer"], "PRD-7")
        self.assertTrue(llm.image.startswith("data:image/png;base64,"))
        self.assertEqual(await g.sweep(evaluate, gates=False), 0)  # never between steps

    async def test_page_change_counter_tells_each_consumer_once(self):
        g = guard.PopupGuard(NS(llm=None), "a")
        states = iter([{"seq": 1, "fresh": True}, {"seq": 1}, {"seq": 2}, {"seq": 2}, {"seq": 2}, {"seq": 1, "fresh": True},
                       {"seq": 1}])

        async def evaluate(js, *args):
            self.assertIn("MutationObserver", js)
            return next(states)
        self.assertTrue(await g.changed(evaluate, "action"))       # new document
        self.assertTrue(await g.changed(evaluate, "loop"))         # first look of this consumer
        self.assertTrue(await g.changed(evaluate, "action"))       # a block-like change
        self.assertFalse(await g.changed(evaluate, "action"))

        tools = GuardedTools()

            ran.append(name)
            return "not executed: a gate covered the page"

        async def evaluate(js, *args):

content.text:
Run F failed with **quality 10**: it signed a bid with all 5 positions left out. I found the cause, fixed it and started run H. Run G is still running and stalls the same way, so it will very likely score low too.

**What went wrong in F:**
- **Missing data:** the ERP produced 0 pages and the spec produced 4 pages with no requirements, so no material could be matched.
- **Stalls:** there were no model calls and no browser actions from 1:00 to 2:30, and again from 3:16 to 4:41. All browsers hit 30 s page-state timeouts at the same time.
- **Lost spec:** browser 1 (spec) died and its agent moved to the ERP browser, which then stalled too. The ERP agent waited 464 s for requirements that never came.
- **Cause:** our page-script helper (`_evaluate`) opened a new browser connection on every call and never closed it. Each one received all of that tab's network traffic. The real-time guard calls it twice a second per agent, so hundreds of connections piled up and the browsers stopped answering. Run E had the same leak at a slower rate, which probably explains its timeouts during the TAN.
- **What still worked:** the TAN took 84 s from request to receipt, down from 238 s in E; the reload-after-unlock rule worked. The wizard took 142 s with every position left out.

**Fixes:**
- **`_evaluate`** (`swarm/browser_agent.py`) now reuses the agent's existing browser connection, so a poll costs one small call.
- **`WATCH_JS`** (`swarm/guard.py`), the in-page change watcher, now only queues changed elements and checks at most 60 of them at each poll. It no longer forces page layout on every change. Pages that contain an iframe (mail reader, Q&A) no longer count as changed whenever any class changes.
- I checked the watcher in a real Chromium page: a class change gives no trigger, while a new dialog or a fixed overlay does. The new connection reuse is covered by a unit test but has not run in a real browser yet; run H is the first real check. All 181 unit tests pass.

**Running:**
- **G** (`reh_3d75a2747df66520`): includes the leak.
- **H** (`reh_0699a5be6a22e759`): G plus both fixes.

Both are watched in the background; I'll pull their logs and compare them with E (quality 96.1, 18:42) when they finish. F's analysis is in `INDEX.md` and `reh_3d86cd104c8eb1b5.md`. Nothing is committed.

async def _enable_page_monitoring_routed(self, cdp_session) -> None:
    """browser-use registers one lifecycle handler per page target, but the CDP client keeps only ONE handler per event
    (the last one), and that handler drops events of every other target. With several tabs in a browser, navigations
    in all but the last-attached tab then waited for load events that never came (3-8 s per navigation). Here one
    handler per client routes each event to the queue of its own target."""
    await _enable_page_monitoring(self, cdp_session)
    events = getattr(cdp_session, "_lifecycle_events", None)
    if events is None:
        return
    routes = self.__dict__.setdefault("_lifecycle_routes", {})
    routes[cdp_session.target_id] = events

    def route(event, session_id=None):
        target = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if session_id else None
        queue = routes.get(target)
        if queue is not None:
            queue.append({"name": event.get("name", "unknown"), "loaderId": event.get("loaderId", "none"),
                          "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()})

    cdp_session.cdp_client.register.Page.lifecycleEvent(route)


SessionManager._enable_page_monitoring = _enable_page_monitoring_routed


class RobustSession(BrowserSession):
    """A BrowserSession whose navigation recovers from a tab stuck while loading: stop the old load and retry once.
    It works in its own `Tab` (set `_tab` before starting), with focus emulation on: with several windows only one has
    the OS focus, and in the others typed text and focus-dependent page scripts did nothing (logins "did not register",
    links "did not navigate"). Playwright enables the same emulation on every page for this reason."""

    _tab: Any = PrivateAttr(default=None)
    _focus_emulated: set = PrivateAttr(default_factory=set)
    _dialogs_handled: set = PrivateAttr(default_factory=set)
    _state_timeouts: int = PrivateAttr(default=0)
    _dialog_tasks: set = PrivateAttr(default_factory=set)
    _dialog_pending: dict = PrivateAttr(default_factory=dict)

    async def get_browser_state_summary(self, include_screenshot: bool = True, cached: bool = False,
                                        include_recent_events: bool = False):
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(30):
                state = await super().get_browser_state_summary(
                    include_screenshot=include_screenshot, cached=cached, include_recent_events=include_recent_events)
            self._state_timeouts = 0
            return state
        except TimeoutError as error:
            self._state_timeouts += 1
            raise RuntimeError('Browser state capture timed out after 30s; retry observation before acting') from error

    async def connect(self, cdp_url: str | None = None):
        await super().connect(cdp_url)
        tab, focus = self._tab, self.agent_focus_target_id
        if tab is not None and focus and tab.target_id != focus:
            alive = {t.target_id for t in _all_page_targets(self.session_manager)}
            if tab.target_id not in alive:      # a main tab's first use, or the agent closed its tab: adopt this one
                _OWNERS.pop(tab.target_id or "", None)
                tab.popups.discard(focus)
                tab.claim(focus)
        if tab is not None and focus:
            await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(focus, focus=True)     # turns focus emulation on for the tab
        return self

    async def get_or_create_cdp_session(self, target_id=None, focus: bool = True):
        session = await super().get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=focus)
        if focus and self._tab is not None:
            self._tab.adopt(session.target_id)      # the agent went into a popup of its tab: keep others out
        if focus and self._tab is not None and session.session_id not in self._focus_emulated:
            self._focus_emulated.add(session.session_id)
            try:
                await session.cdp_client.send.Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(
                    params={"enabled": True}, session_id=session.session_id)
            except Exception as error:
                log.debug("focus emulation failed: %s", error)
        if focus and session.session_id not in self._dialogs_handled:
            self._dialogs_handled.add(session.session_id)
            await self._handle_dialogs(session)
        return session

    async def _handle_dialogs(self, session) -> None:
        """Accept native JavaScript dialogs (alert, confirm such as "submit binding bid?", beforeunload) in the agent's
        tab. browser-use registers this per new tab, but its handler missed the bid wizard's final confirm: the page
        then froze, every page script and state read waited for the dialog, and the run ended without an answer."""
        root = self._cdp_client_root or session.cdp_client

        async def dismiss(event, session_id=None):
            kind, message = event.get("type", "alert"), event.get("message", "")
            try:
                self._closed_popup_messages.append(f"[{kind}] {message}")
            except Exception:
                pass
            log.info("accepting %s dialog: %s", kind, message[:120])
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(root.send.Page.handleJavaScriptDialog(
                    params={"accept": kind != "prompt"}, session_id=session_id or session.session_id), 5)
                return True
            except Exception as error:
                log.debug("dialog handling failed: %s", error)
                return False

        def target_for(session_id):
            manager = self.session_manager
            return (manager.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if manager and session_id else None) or getattr(session, "target_id", session_id)

        def on_closed(event, session_id=None):
            target = target_for(session_id or session.session_id)
            for key in list(self._dialog_pending):
                if key[0] == target:
                    self._dialog_pending.pop(key, None)

        def on_dialog(event, session_id=None):
            # cdp-use awaits async callbacks inside its sole WebSocket receive loop. Waiting for a CDP
            # response there prevents that very response from being received and stalls page observation.
            key = (target_for(session_id or session.session_id), event.get("type"), event.get("message"))
            if key in self._dialog_pending:
                return
            task = asyncio.create_task(dismiss(event, session_id))
            self._dialog_pending[key] = task
            self._dialog_tasks.add(task)
            def finished(done):
                self._dialog_tasks.discard(done)
                if done.cancelled() or done.exception() or not done.result():
                    if self._dialog_pending.get(key) is done:
                        self._dialog_pending.pop(key, None)
            task.add_done_callback(finished)
        try:
            session.cdp_client.register.Page.javascriptDialogOpening(on_dialog)
            session.cdp_client.register.Page.javascriptDialogClosed(on_closed)
            await session.cdp_client.send.Page.enable(session_id=session.session_id)
        except Exception as error:
            log.debug("dialog handler not registered: %s", error)

    async def _navigate_and_wait(self, url, target_id, timeout=None, wait_until="load"):
        try:
            return await super()._navigate_and_wait(url, target_id, timeout=timeout, wait_until=wait_until)
        except RuntimeError as error:
            if "timed out" not in str(error):
                raise
            log.warning("navigation stuck, stopping the old load and retrying: %s", url)
            session = await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=False)
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(session.cdp_client.send.Page.stopLoading(session_id=session.session_id), 5)
            except Exception as stop_error:
                log.debug("stopLoading failed: %s", stop_error)
            return await super()._navigate_and_wait(url, target_id, timeout=timeout, wait_until=wait_until)

    session = self.browser_session
    if isinstance(session, RobustSession):
        cdp = await session.get_or_create_cdp_session(event.target_id, focus=False)
        await session._handle_dialogs(cdp)
    else:
        await _original_popup_setup(self, event)

def make_session(ctx, tab: Tab, vision: bool = False) -> BrowserSession:
    """Attach to `tab` of the run's CDP browser (locally browser-use starts its own Chromium; HEADLESS=1 hides it)."""
    urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
    cls = RobustSession if vision else TextSession
    profile = dict(allowed_domains=allowed_domains(ctx.task), enable_default_extensions=False, keep_alive=True)
    if urls:
        session = cls(cdp_url=urls[tab.browser % len(urls)], **profile)
        session._tab = tab
        return session
    return cls(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1", window_size={"width": 1280, "height": 800}, **profile)

await self._cdp_client_root.start()

			# Initialize event-driven session manager FIRST (before enabling autoAttach)
			# SessionManager will:
			# 1. Register attach/detach event handlers
			# 2. Discover and attach to all existing targets
			# 3. Initialize sessions and enable lifecycle monitoring
			# 4. Enable autoAttach for future targets
			from browser_use.browser.session_manager import SessionManager

			self.session_manager = SessionManager(self)
			await self.session_manager.start_monitoring()
			self.logger.debug('Event-driven session manager started')

			# Enable auto-attach so Chrome automatically notifies us when NEW targets attach/detach
			# This is the foundation of event-driven session management
			await self._cdp_client_root.send.Target.setAutoAttach(
				params={'autoAttach': True, 'waitForDebuggerOnStart': False, 'flatten': True}
			)
			self.logger.debug('CDP client connected with auto-attach enabled')

			# Get browser targets from SessionManager (source of truth)
			# SessionManager has already discovered all targets via start_monitoring()
			page_targets_from_manager = self.session_manager.get_all_page_targets()

			# Check for chrome://newtab pages and redirect them to about:blank (in parallel)
			from browser_use.utils import is_new_tab_page

			async def _redirect_newtab(target):
				target_url = target.url
				target_id = target.target_id
				self.logger.debug(f'🔄 Redirecting {target_url} to about:blank for target {target_id}')
				try:
					session = await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=False)
					await session.cdp_client.send.Page.navigate(params={'url': 'about:blank'}, session_id=session.session_id)
					target.url = 'about:blank'
				except Exception as e:
					self.logger.warning(f'Failed to redirect {target_url}: {e}')

			redirect_tasks = [
				_redirect_newtab(target)
				for target in page_targets_from_manager
				if is_new_tab_page(target.url) and target.url != 'about:blank'
			]

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Run the swarm (or some agents) locally against the public scouting sites, headless, and save the whole log as
  Markdown in .swarm/local/ (git-ignored, never packaged). Nothing entered with scouting logins counts.

  Needs `atira models proxy` running (the local Qwen proxy). Locally every browse starts its own Chromium.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\local-run.ps1 -Only "BriefReader,BidSubmitter" -Name submitter
  .\scripts\local-run.ps1 -Only "BriefReader,MailScraper,DiscountAnalyzer" -Name mail -Board .swarm/board.json
#>
param(
    [string]$Only = "",          # SWARM_ONLY: comma-separated agent names (empty = whole swarm)
    [string]$Name = "local",     # label for the log file
    [string]$Board = "",         # SWARM_BOARD_IN: start from a saved board (skip scraping that is already done)
    [switch]$Visible             # show the browsers (default headless)
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force ".swarm/local" | Out-Null
$stamp = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyyMMdd-HHmm")
$log = ".swarm/local/$stamp-$Name.md"

atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
$env:SWARM_ONLY = $Only
$env:SWARM_BOARD_IN = $Board
$env:HEADLESS = if ($Visible) { "0" } else { "1" }
$env:PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"

Set-Content -Encoding utf8 $log ("# Local run $stamp ($Name)`n`nSWARM_ONLY=$Only; SWARM_BOARD_IN=$Board`n`n" + '```text')
cmd /c "uv run --no-sync python agent.py 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { Add-Content -Encoding utf8 $log $_ }
Add-Content -Encoding utf8 $log '```'
Write-Host "log: $log"
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page

"""Benchmark: browser-use state capture cost vs number of concurrent sessions on one browser (sandbox-like CDP)."""
import asyncio, json, os, subprocess, sys, time, statistics
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

PORT = 9333
URL = os.environ["CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL"]
K = int(os.environ.get("K", "8"))

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        exe = p.chromium.executable_path
    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe, f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--headless=new", "--no-first-run",
                             f"--user-data-dir={os.environ['TEMP']}/bench/prof", "about:blank"],
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    os.environ["CDP_URLS"] = json.dumps([f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}"])
    from browser_use import BrowserSession
    from swarm.browser_agent import TextSession
    try:
        # K tabs on the site
        async with async_playwright() as p:
            b = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}")
            ctx = b.contexts[0]
            pages = [ctx.pages[0]] + [await ctx.new_page() for _ in range(K - 1)]
            await asyncio.gather(*(pg.goto(URL, wait_until="load") for pg in pages))
            cdp = await ctx.new_cdp_session(pages[0])
            targets = [t["targetId"] for t in (await cdp.send("Target.getTargets"))["targetInfos"] if t["type"] == "page"]
            print("tabs", len(targets), "url", pages[0].url[:40], "html chars", len(await pages[0].content()))
            JS = "() => ({t: document.body.innerText.length, n: document.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,select,textarea').length})"
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(5):
                await pages[0].evaluate(JS)
            print(f"one JS snapshot evaluate: {(time.perf_counter()-t0)/5*1000:.1f} ms")

            async def session_for(tid):
                s = TextSession(cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}", keep_alive=True)
                t = time.perf_counter()
                await s.start()
                await s.get_or_create_cdp_session(tid, focus=True)
                return s, time.perf_counter() - t

            async def capture(s, n=3):
                out = []
                for _ in range(n):
                    t = time.perf_counter()
                    await s.get_browser_state_summary(include_screenshot=False)
                    out.append(time.perf_counter() - t)
                return out

            s1, c1 = await session_for(targets[0])
            print(f"1 session: connect {c1:.2f}s, attached sessions {len(s1.session_manager._session_to_target)}")
            caps = await capture(s1, 5)
            print("1 session capture s:", [round(x, 2) for x in caps])
            await s1.kill() if hasattr(s1, "kill") else None
            sess = await asyncio.gather(*(session_for(t) for t in targets[:K]))
            print(f"{K} sessions: connect s {[round(c,2) for _,c in sess]}, attached per session "
                  f"{[len(s.session_manager._session_to_target) for s,_ in sess]}")
            caps = await asyncio.gather(*(capture(s) for s, _ in sess))
            flat = [x for c in caps for x in c]
            print(f"{K} concurrent captures s: median {statistics.median(flat):.2f} max {max(flat):.2f}")
    finally:
        proc.kill()

asyncio.run(main())
EOF

async def on_BrowserStateRequestEvent(self, event: BrowserStateRequestEvent) -> None:
		"""Handle browser state request events."""
		# Use public API - automatically validates and waits for recovery if needed
		self.logger.debug(f'[DownloadsWatchdog] on_BrowserStateRequestEvent started, event_id={event.event_id[-4:]}')
		try:
			cdp_session = await self.browser_session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
		except ValueError:
			self.logger.warning(f'[DownloadsWatchdog] No valid focus, skipping BrowserStateRequestEvent {event.event_id[-4:]}')

entries.description: Every model call of a run, one line each: time on the run's clock, latency, queue wait (hosted models), model, status, tokens (cached), cost and id. The header has the time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and the hosted models' queue waits. Filter by from/to, model and status (ok, error, all); page with after. About 35 tokens a call.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest start, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest start, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

model.description: Only models whose provider/model contains this, e.g. qwen

after.description: Continue after a call id (c_123), e.g. the previous page's next

"""Navigation cost (readiness waits) with 1 vs K sessions on one browser, and fetch() of pages in page context."""
import asyncio, json, os, subprocess, sys, time, logging, statistics
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
PORT = 9334
URLS = [os.environ[k] for k in ("CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL", "CHALLENGE_SITE_MAIL_URL", "CHALLENGE_SITE_ERP_URL",
                                "CHALLENGE_SITE_CUSTOMER_PORTAL_URL")]
K = int(os.environ.get("K", "8"))
warn = []
class H(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, r):
        if "readiness timeout" in r.getMessage(): warn.append(r.getMessage())

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        exe = p.chromium.executable_path
    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe, f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--headless=new", "--no-first-run",
                             f"--user-data-dir={os.environ['TEMP']}/bench/prof2", "about:blank"],
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    os.environ["CDP_URLS"] = json.dumps([f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}"])
    from swarm.browser_agent import TextSession
    logging.getLogger("browser_use").addHandler(H())
    try:
        async with async_playwright() as p:
            b = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}")
            ctx = b.contexts[0]
            pages = [ctx.pages[0]] + [await ctx.new_page() for _ in range(K - 1)]
            cdp = await ctx.new_cdp_session(pages[0])
            targets = [t["targetId"] for t in (await cdp.send("Target.getTargets"))["targetInfos"] if t["type"] == "page"]

            async def session_for(tid):
                s = TextSession(cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}", keep_alive=True)
                await s.start()
                await s.get_or_create_cdp_session(tid, focus=True)
                return s

            async def navs(s, n=4):
                out = []
                for i in range(n):
                    t = time.perf_counter()
                    await s.navigate_to(URLS[i % len(URLS)])
                    out.append(time.perf_counter() - t)
                return out

            for k in (1, K):
                warn.clear()
                sess = await asyncio.gather(*(session_for(t) for t in targets[:k]))
                res = await asyncio.gather(*(navs(s) for s in sess))
                flat = [x for r in res for x in r]
                print(f"{k} sessions: navigate s median {statistics.median(flat):.2f} max {max(flat):.2f}; "
                      f"readiness timeouts {len(warn)}/{len(flat)}", flush=True)
                for s in sess:
                    try: await asyncio.wait_for(s.stop(), 5)
                    except Exception: pass
            # fetch() several same-origin pages inside one page (cookies of the tab)
            await pages[0].goto(URLS[1])
            t = time.perf_counter()
            sizes = await pages[0].evaluate("""async (u) => Promise.all(Array.from({length: 8}, (_, i) =>
                fetch(u + '?x=' + i, {credentials: 'include'}).then(r => r.text()).then(t => t.length)))""", URLS[1])
            print(f"fetch 8 pages in page context: {time.perf_counter()-t:.2f}s sizes {sizes[:3]}", flush=True)
    finally:
        proc.kill()
asyncio.run(main())
EOF
echo ok

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    try:
        async with async_playwright() as playwright:
            answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    except Exception as error:
        logging.getLogger("agent").error("Workflow failed: %s", error)
        return 1
    if answer is None:
        print("Portal submission confirmed; no API answer to post"
              if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else "No answer to submit", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

async def __aexit__(self, *exc):

class TheEntryPoint(Case):
    """main() with a fake swarm: no answer exits cleanly, an answer is submitted."""

    async def start(self, environment, answer=None):
        async def solve(task, playwright, scored):
            self.seen = (task, scored)
            return answer

        out = io.StringIO()
        with patch.dict(os.environ, environment, clear=True), \
                patch.object(agent, "solve", solve), \
                patch.object(agent, "async_playwright", FakePlaywright), redirect_stdout(out):
            code = await agent.main()
        return code, out.getvalue()

    async def test_without_an_answer_it_exits_cleanly(self):
        api = self.serve({"/v1/runs/current": [(200, RUN)]})
        code, out = await self.start({"CHALLENGE_API_URL": api.url, "CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN": "rt_secret"})
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.seen, (RUN, True))
        self.assertIn("No answer to submit", out)
        self.assertEqual([request["method"] for request in api.requests], ["GET"])
        self.assertNotIn("s3cret", out)

def lookup_found(task: asyncio.Task) -> bool:
    """A finished TAN lookup that read a TAN (else a new lookup starts)."""
    if task.cancelled() or task.exception() is not None:
        return False
    return str(task.result()).startswith("TAN:")


class ReceiptParams(BaseModel):
    quote: str = Field(description="Exact text on the current portal page confirming the bid was submitted, not saved as draft")
    reference: str = Field(description="Tender reference for this receipt")


RECEIPT_REJECT_BELOW = 0.3      # only a clear "no" blocks: the portal may have accepted the bid already


async def looks_unsubmitted(page_text: str, quote: str) -> bool:
    """Clef's second opinion on a receipt the submitter quotes: True only when the page clearly is not one (a draft
    save or review page quoted too early). Without Clef, or when it is slow, the quote check alone decides."""
    from swarm import decide
    if not decide.available():
        return False
    try:
        answers = await asyncio.wait_for(decide.decide(
            {"page": page_text[:3000], "quoted_as_receipt": quote[:300]},
            {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does this page confirm that the bid/offer was submitted bindingly "
                                                   "(a receipt or confirmation), not saved as draft, not a "
                                                   "review/summary, form or error page?"}}, retries=0), 15)
        p = float(answers["q"]["noul"])
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return False
    return p < RECEIPT_REJECT_BELOW

            "binding submission (accept browser dialog). done once portal confirms submission; report "
            "confirmation/receipt text. Call confirm_submission with an exact quote from the portal receipt before done. "
            "get_signing_tan waits for the TAN itself; if it reports still running, call it again at once (no wait "
            "action, no other step); do not request another TAN. "
            "A failed attempt may already have submitted: inspect current portal status before any new binding action. "
            "On the summary/review page call check_entries once (it compares the page with the values above); fix "
            "what it reports missing before confirming; no need to read_page the summary yourself.")
        prepared = ctx.shared.get("wizard_ready")
        if prepared:
            goal += (f"\n\nPREPARED: this tab is already logged in and in the bid wizard for this tender (nothing entered "
                     f"yet). What the preparation saw: {str(prepared)[:400]}")

        tan_requested = asyncio.Event()
        # The TAN lookup starts now, in standby: it logs the mail browser in, passes its gate, opens the inbox and then
        # waits (wait_for_tan_request) until the submitter requests the TAN. Run C lost ~139 s between request and
        # entry: lookup start, gate fights and the submitter polling get_signing_tan once per model step.
        tan_task = asyncio.create_task(self.tan_lookup(mail_site, answer, started, tan_requested, standby=True))
        expected = expected_values(bid)

        def tan_tool(tools):
            @tools.action("Check the current page (bid summary) against the values to enter; lists what is missing.",
                          param_model=CheckParams)
            async def check_entries(params: CheckParams, browser_session: BrowserSession):
                text = await read_current_page(browser_session)
                missing = check_page(text, expected)
                await ctx.board.set("submission_check", {"missing": missing, "checked": sum(map(len, expected.values())),
                                                         "note": params.note})
                timeline.mark("entries checked", missing=len(missing))
                if missing:
                    return ActionResult(extracted_content="NOT on this page (fix before confirming): " + "; ".join(missing),
                                        long_term_memory="check_entries: missing " + "; ".join(missing)[:300])
                return ActionResult(extracted_content=f"All {sum(map(len, expected.values()))} expected values are on "
                                                      "this page.", long_term_memory="check_entries: all values present")

            @tools.action("Confirm acceptance using an exact receipt quote on the current portal page.", param_model=ReceiptParams)
            async def confirm_submission(params: ReceiptParams, browser_session: BrowserSession):
                from swarm.normalize import norm_ref
                from urllib.parse import urlsplit
                current_url = await browser_session.get_current_page_url()
                if urlsplit(current_url).netloc != urlsplit(site["url"]).netloc:
                    return ActionResult(error="Acceptance must be confirmed on the tender portal")
                observed = await read_current_page(browser_session)
                quote = " ".join(params.quote.split())
                expected = answer.get("tender_reference") or facts.get("tender_reference")
                if not expected or norm_ref(params.reference) != norm_ref(expected):
                    return ActionResult(error="Receipt reference does not match this tender")
                if len(quote) < 12 or quote not in " ".join(observed.split()):
                    return ActionResult(error="Receipt quote is not on the current page; read the portal confirmation")
                if await looks_unsubmitted(observed, quote):
                    return ActionResult(error="This page does not look like a binding submission receipt (draft, "
                                              "review or form?). Finish the submission, then confirm on the receipt.")
                receipt = {"accepted": True, "reference": expected, "quote": quote,
                           "url": await browser_session.get_current_page_url()}
                await ctx.board.set("submission", receipt)
                await ctx.board.post(Evidence("submission.receipt", tender_site, receipt, source=receipt["url"], author=self.name))
                timeline.mark("accepted submission", left=round(ctx.seconds_left()))
                timeline.current().log_report()        # the run (and this process) ends within seconds
                return ActionResult(extracted_content="Receipt recorded; finish now", is_done=True, success=True)

            @tools.action("Read newest signing TAN from our webmail (call right after requesting TAN). Waits for it "
                          "and returns the TAN as soon as the mail is read.", param_model=TanParams)
            async def get_signing_tan(params: TanParams):
                nonlocal tan_task
                if timeline.mark("TAN requested", left=round(ctx.seconds_left())):
                    timeline.current().log_report()   # the run ends soon after the TAN is entered: report it now

async def responsive_tab(tab: "Tab") -> "Tab":
    """The tab to work in: `tab` if its browser answers, else a new tab of the next browser that does. Any browser can
    open any site, so one dead browser must not take a whole role (or the signing) down with it. A healthy tab of a
    browser checked within CHECK_EVERY_S skips the check (it cost every browse a CDP round trip)."""
    urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
    if not urls:
        return tab
    if tab.replacement is not None:          # work already moved to another browser: keep using that tab
        return await responsive_tab(tab.replacement)
    recent = time.monotonic() - _CHECKED.get(tab.browser, -1e9) < CHECK_EVERY_S
    if recent and not tab.suspect:
        return tab
    with timeline.span("recovery", f"check browser {tab.browser}"):
        if await browser_responds(tab.browser):
            closed = await close_hung_tabs(tab.browser, mine=tab)
            if closed:
                timeline.count("tabs.hung_closed", len(closed))
            else:
                _CHECKED[tab.browser] = time.monotonic()
            if tab.target_id and tab.target_id in closed:
                now = time.monotonic()
                recent = [t for t in _HUNG_AT.get(tab.browser, []) if now - t < REPEAT_HANG_S]
                _HUNG_AT[tab.browser] = recent + [now]
                timeline.count("tabs.replaced")
                if recent:            # hung again on this browser (run_db181692d8232b97: twice while signing)
                    others = [(len([t for t in _HUNG_AT.get(b, []) if now - t < REPEAT_HANG_S]), b)
                              for b in range(len(urls)) if b != tab.browser]
                    for _, other in sorted(others):
                        if await browser_responds(other):
                            log.warning("browser %d hung again: continuing in a new tab of browser %d",
                                        tab.browser, other)
                            timeline.count("tabs.moved_browser")
                            tab.renew()
                            tab.replacement = Tab(other)      # closed together with `tab` by its owner
                            return tab.replacement
                log.warning("browser %d: this agent's tab was hung and closed; continuing in a new tab", tab.browser)
                tab.renew()           # same Tab object: its owner still closes it, and a main tab stays the main tab
            tab.suspect = False
            return tab
        for step in range(1, len(urls)):
            other = (tab.browser + step) % len(urls)
            if await browser_responds(other):
                log.warning("browser %d is unreachable: continuing in a new tab of browser %d", tab.browser, other)
                timeline.count("tabs.moved_browser")
                moved = Tab(other)

                return moved
