def main_tab(browser: int) -> Tab:
    return _MAIN_TABS.setdefault(browser, Tab(browser, main=True))


_OPENERS: dict[str, str] = {}      # target id -> id of the target that opened it (popups), from Chrome's target info


def owner_of(target_id: str) -> Tab | None:
    """The tab a target belongs to: its own claim, else the owner of the tab that opened it (popup of a popup too)."""
    seen = set()
    while target_id and target_id not in seen:
        seen.add(target_id)
        if target_id in _OWNERS:
            return _OWNERS[target_id]
        target_id = _OPENERS.get(target_id, "")
    return None


_all_page_targets = SessionManager.get_all_page_targets


def _visible_page_targets(self) -> list:
    """What a session sees as "the browser's tabs": its own tab first, then popups its pages opened; never another
    agent's tab or popups. A tab nobody owns and no owned tab opened (the browser's first tab) is visible only to the
    browser's main tab, which claims it. browser-use derives its tab list, focus and new-tab reuse from this."""
    targets = _all_page_targets(self)
    tab = getattr(self.browser_session, "_tab", None)
    if tab is None:
        return targets
    mine = [t for t in targets if t.target_id == tab.target_id]
    rest = [t for t in targets if t.target_id != tab.target_id
            and (owner_of(t.target_id) is tab or (owner_of(t.target_id) is None and tab.main))]
    return mine + rest

    info = event.get("targetInfo") or {}

ISOLATE_TABS = os.environ.get("SWARM_ISOLATE_TABS", "1") != "0"


def _sees(tab: "Tab", target_id: str) -> bool:
    """Does the session working in `tab` see this page target? Same rule as _visible_page_targets."""
    owner = owner_of(target_id)
    return target_id == tab.target_id or owner is tab or (owner is None and tab.main)


async def _handle_target_attached_with_opener(self, event) -> None:
    """Record popup openers, and keep each agent's connection to its own pages. browser-use attaches every session to
    EVERY tab of the browser and enables Page, lifecycle and Network events on each: with 8 agents in one browser
    every navigation's events went to all 8 connections, and a navigation took 40 s instead of 0.4 s (local
    benchmark, 8 sessions on 16 tabs; the ERP browser in the sandbox ran 8 tabs). A foreign page is detached at
    once, before any domain is enabled; its frames then never attach either."""
    info = event.get("targetInfo") or {}
    if info.get("openerId"):
        _OPENERS[info["targetId"]] = info["openerId"]
    tab = getattr(self.browser_session, "_tab", None)
    if ISOLATE_TABS and tab is not None and info.get("type") == "page" and not _sees(tab, info.get("targetId", "")):
        root = self.browser_session._cdp_client_root
        if root is not None and event.get("sessionId"):
            try:
                await root.send.Target.detachFromTarget(params={"sessionId": event["sessionId"]})
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the tab closed meanwhile
                log.debug("detach from a foreign tab failed: %s", error)
        return
    await _handle_target_attached(self, event)

"""Navigation + state capture with K agents' sessions on one browser, as the swarm creates them (Tab + TextSession)."""
import asyncio, json, os, subprocess, sys, time, logging, statistics
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
PORT = int(os.environ.get("PORT", "9335"))
URLS = [os.environ[k] for k in ("CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL", "CHALLENGE_SITE_MAIL_URL", "CHALLENGE_SITE_ERP_URL",
                                "CHALLENGE_SITE_CUSTOMER_PORTAL_URL")]
K = int(os.environ.get("K", "8"))
warn = []
class H(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, r):
        m = r.getMessage()
        if "readiness timeout" in m or "Initialization timeout" in m: warn.append(m)

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        exe = p.chromium.executable_path
    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe, f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--headless=new", "--no-first-run",
                             f"--user-data-dir={os.environ['TEMP']}/bench/prof{PORT}", "about:blank"],
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    os.environ["CDP_URLS"] = json.dumps([f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}"])
    from swarm import browser_agent as ba
    logging.getLogger("browser_use").addHandler(H())
    print("isolate", ba.ISOLATE_TABS, flush=True)
    try:
        tabs = [ba.Tab(0) for _ in range(K)]
        for t in tabs:
            await t.open()

        async def session_for(tab):
            s = ba.TextSession(cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}", keep_alive=True)
            s._tab = tab
            t = time.perf_counter()
            await s.start()
            await s.get_or_create_cdp_session(tab.target_id, focus=True)
            return s, time.perf_counter() - t

        async def work(s, n=4):
            navs, caps = [], []
            for i in range(n):
                t = time.perf_counter()
                await s.navigate_to(URLS[i % len(URLS)])
                navs.append(time.perf_counter() - t)
                t = time.perf_counter()
                await s.get_browser_state_summary(include_screenshot=False)
                caps.append(time.perf_counter() - t)
            return navs, caps

        sess = await asyncio.gather(*(session_for(t) for t in tabs))
        print(f"{K} sessions connect s median {statistics.median([c for _, c in sess]):.2f}; attached per session "
              f"{[len(s.session_manager._session_to_target) for s, _ in sess]}", flush=True)
        res = await asyncio.gather(*(work(s) for s, _ in sess))
        navs = [x for r in res for x in r[0]]; caps = [x for r in res for x in r[1]]
        print(f"navigate median {statistics.median(navs):.2f} max {max(navs):.2f}; capture median "
              f"{statistics.median(caps):.2f} max {max(caps):.2f}; timeouts {len(warn)}", flush=True)
    finally:
        proc.kill()
asyncio.run(main())
EOF

        s = ba.TextSession(cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}", keep_alive=True); s._tab = tab

        print("targets", {t[:6]: v.target_type for t, v in sm._targets.items()})

        proc.kill()

		cdp_session = await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=False)

		if timeout is None:
			target = self.session_manager.get_target(target_id)
			current_url = target.url
			same_domain = (
				url.split('/')[2] == current_url.split('/')[2]
				if url.startswith('http') and current_url.startswith('http')
				else False
			)
			timeout = 3.0 if same_domain else 8.0

		nav_start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()

		# Wrap Page.navigate() with timeout — heavy sites can block here for 10s+
		nav_timeout = 20.0
		try:
			nav_result = await asyncio.wait_for(
				cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Page.navigate(
					params={'url': url, 'transitionType': 'address_bar'},
					session_id=cdp_session.session_id,
				),
				timeout=nav_timeout,
			)
		except TimeoutError:
			duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
			raise RuntimeError(f'Page.navigate() timed out after {nav_timeout}s ({duration_ms:.0f}ms) for {url}')

		if nav_result.get('errorText'):
			raise RuntimeError(f'Navigation failed: {nav_result["errorText"]}')

		if wait_until == 'commit':
			duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
			self.logger.debug(f'✅ Page ready for {url} (commit, {duration_ms:.0f}ms)')
			return

		navigation_id = nav_result.get('loaderId')
		start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
		seen_events = []

content.text:
The benchmark is finished; each pass took about 2 minutes. I haven't started anything else.

The test simulates the ERP browser: 8 agents in 8 tabs of one browser, each loading 4 site pages and capturing the page state the model reads after each load. "Load wait" is how long browser-use waits for a page to be reported as loaded.

| Setup | Load time (median / max) | Page-state capture (median / max) | Load waits that timed out |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original code (earlier test) | 17 s / 26 s | 9 s / 18 s | 12 |
| Fix 1 (page-load events) | 1.4 s / 3.1 s | 1.1 s / 2.7 s | 0 |
| Fix 1 + fix 2 (own tab only) | 1.2 s / 2.0 s | 0.9 s / 1.9 s | 0 |

A single agent alone in a browser loads a page in 0.35 s.

What the two fixes are:
1. **Page-load events** (`swarm/browser_agent.py`): each tab has two connections from browser-use, and our code sent the "page loaded" signal to only one of them. About half of all page loads waited the full 3–8 s for a signal that never came. This explains the "Page readiness timeout" warning in every sandbox log. Both connections now get the signal. This is the big win.
2. **Own tab only** (on by default, switch off with `SWARM_ISOLATE_TABS=0`): each agent's connection used to attach to every tab in its browser, 23 connections each in the test. Now it attaches to its own tab, 7 each. This gives a smaller extra gain.

Also changed since run H, all aimed at run G's failures:
- **Hard exit:** the process now exits at the end and at the deadline. G hung 6 minutes past its end until you cancelled it.
- **Contact email:** the submitter now gets the bidder's email from the webmail login. In G it got stuck 10 minutes on the required email field.
- **TAN guard:** `get_signing_tan` is refused until `check_entries` has run on the summary page. In G it was called on wizard step 1, and the TAN lookup then reloaded an empty inbox for 10 minutes.

Run H (CDP leak fixed) had 0 page-state timeouts and no browser crashes, but scored only 26.5 with 1 of 5 positions. The ERP was too slow, and these fixes target that.

**Still open:** the unit tests haven't been run since these changes; you stopped that run. The TAN guard may break an existing submitter test that calls `get_signing_tan` without `check_entries`. Next would be to run the tests, then a sandbox run. Shall I go ahead?

async def fake_extract(ctx, instruction, shape, blocks, **kwargs):
            if 'quick' in blocks[0]:
                return {'revisions':[{'revision':'C','is_current':True}],
                        'requirements':[{'ref':'X','revision':'C','bore':'73'}]}
            await asyncio.Event().wait()
        with patch.object(analyze_requirements, 'extract', fake_extract):
            task = asyncio.create_task(analyze_requirements.analyse(ctx))
            result = await ctx.board.wait_for(key='requirements', timeout=2)
            self.assertEqual(result['X']['bore'], '73')
            self.assertFalse(task.done())
            task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(task, return_exceptions=True)

    async def test_contradicted_complete_site_mapping_is_replaced(self):
        from swarm.sites import resolve_roles
        class LLM:
            async def ask_json(self, *args, **kwargs): return {'erp':'second'}
        ctx = Context(task={'brief':'','access':[{'siteId':'first'},{'siteId':'second'}]},
                      board=Blackboard(), llm=LLM(), pool=None)
        ctx.board.results['sites'] = dict.fromkeys(('tender','spec','erp','mail'), 'first')
        ctx.shared['site_invalidations'] = {'erp':{'first'}}
        self.assertEqual((await resolve_roles(ctx))['erp'], 'second')

    async def test_signer_reuses_pending_tan_and_requires_receipt(self):
        from agents import submit_bid
        from swarm.browser_agent import build_tools
        ctx = Context(task={'brief': 'Submit the bid.', 'submission': {'kind':'site'}, 'access':[
            {'siteId':'t','url':'https://t.example'}, {'siteId':'m','url':'https://m.example'}]},
            board=Blackboard(), llm=None, pool=None)
        ctx.board.results.update({'sites': {'tender':'t','spec':'t','erp':'t','mail':'m'},
                                  'brief': {'tender_reference':'FIXTURE'}})
        release = asyncio.Event()
        mail_calls = 0
        portal_calls = 0
        class Session:
            async def get_current_page_url(self): return 'https://t.example/receipt'
        async def page_text(session): return 'Bid FIXTURE successfully submitted. Receipt 56789.'
        async def fake_browse(ctx, goal, **kwargs):
            nonlocal mail_calls, portal_calls
            if kwargs['browser'] == 3:
                mail_calls += 1
                await release.wait()
                await kwargs['on_record']({'kind':'mail.tan','data':{'tan':'753951'},'source':'mail','note':''})
                return {'summary':'TAN recorded', 'done':True, 'steps':1}
            portal_calls += 1
            self.assertIn('Discount percent: 0,00.', goal)
            if portal_calls == 1:
                # A model's done=True alone must never end the signing workflow.
                return {'summary':'Stopped without receipt', 'done':True, 'steps':1}
            tools = build_tools(ctx, 't', 'test', None)
            kwargs['extra_tools'](tools)
            actions = tools.registry.registry.actions
            tan = actions['get_signing_tan'].function
            pending = await tan(params=submit_bid.TanParams())
            self.assertIn('still running', pending.extracted_content)
            release.set()
            result = await tan(params=submit_bid.TanParams())
            self.assertEqual(result.extracted_content, 'TAN: 753951')
            confirm = actions['confirm_submission'].function
            bad = await confirm(params=submit_bid.ReceiptParams(quote='This text was invented',reference='FIXTURE'), browser_session=Session())
            self.assertTrue(bad.error)
            good = await confirm(params=submit_bid.ReceiptParams(quote='Bid FIXTURE successfully submitted.',reference='FIXTURE'), browser_session=Session())
            self.assertTrue(good.success)
            return {'summary':'Confirmed receipt', 'done':True, 'steps':2}
        with patch.object(submit_bid, 'browse', fake_browse), patch.object(submit_bid, 'read_current_page', page_text), \
                patch.object(submit_bid, 'TAN_WAIT_S', 0.2):
            await submit_bid.BidSubmitter(ctx).run()
        self.assertEqual((mail_calls, portal_calls), (1, 2))        # the standby lookup delivered the TAN
        self.assertTrue(ctx.board.get('submission')['accepted'])

Sandbox run I (`reh_06531f76ab5f681e`) is queued and watched in the background. I'll pull its results when it ends. All 181 unit tests pass after updating one submitter test for the new TAN check.

**What run I adds over run H:**
- **Page-load events:** the "page loaded" signal now reaches both of each tab's browser connections. In the local benchmark with 8 agents on one browser, median page load fell from 17 s to 1.4 s, with no load timeouts.
- **Own tab only:** each agent's connection attaches to its own tab, not to every tab in the browser. This took the benchmark to 1.2 s per page load and 0.9 s per page-state capture.
- **Hard exit:** the process ends itself after finishing and at the run deadline, so it can't hang past the end the way G did.
- **Contact email:** the submitter takes the bidder's email from the webmail login if no mail was read that names the mailbox owner.
- **TAN guard:** `get_signing_tan` is refused until `check_entries` has run on the summary page.

**Expected effect:** H's main loss was ERP throughput, with 17 jobs taking 2222 s, so only 1 of 5 positions was priced. The page-load fix should make ERP navigation much faster, since 8 agents share that browser.

**Not yet checked in a real run:**
- The own-tab change has only been tested in the local benchmark, never in the swarm itself. Popups and the shared first tab are the edge cases; `SWARM_ISOLATE_TABS=0` switches it off.
- Wizard speed: G's flash-mode submitter never got past the first wizard step, so we don't know yet how fast it is.

Run G, run H, the benchmark numbers and run I are logged in `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`. Nothing is committed.

   - `SessionManager` auto-attaches to ALL targets: `setAutoAttach` plus `_initialize_existing_targets` attaching every existing target, then waiting up to 2 s for each to be ready.
   - `_enable_page_monitoring` runs `Page.enable`, `setLifecycleEventsEnabled` and `Network.enable` on every page.
   - Each target typically has two sessions (the explicit attach plus Chrome's auto-attach). `_get_session_for_target` picks any session from a set, i.e. at random.
   - `_navigate_and_wait` polls `cdp_session._lifecycle_events` with a 3 s (same domain) or 8 s timeout, then logs "Page readiness timeout".
   - The CDP client allows only one handler per event per client.
   - `Page` actor (`actor/page.py`) `_ensure_session` attaches a new session and enables 4 domains per actor instance.

   **Measured costs:**
   - Hosted Qwen queue wait is p50 about 2–3 s; browse steps took about 12–16 s, so roughly 10 s per step is browser overhead.
   - Benchmarks (scouting sites, local Chromium over CDP with `--remote-debugging-port`):
     - one session: navigation 0.35 s, capture 0.02 s;
     - 8 agents on one browser, original code: navigation median 17 s (40 s in another bench), capture 9 s, many readiness timeouts;
     - after the lifecycle routing fix: 1.43 s / 1.08 s;
     - with tab isolation as well: 1.19 s / 0.90 s, 7 attachments each instead of 23–37;
     - `fetch()` of 8 same-origin pages inside a page: 0.24 s;
     - one JS snapshot evaluate: 6.6 ms.

   **Architecture ideas (not implemented):**
   - A custom JS-snapshot agent loop instead of browser-use DOM capture.
   - In-page `fetch()` for reading model-chosen URLs in parallel.
   - Code-driven wizard filling (one model call per wizard page).
   - Fetch-based TAN polling.
   - Reuse of one `BrowserSession` per Tab across browses.

   **Swarm phases:** COLLECT → VERIFY → COMPUTE → SUBMIT; `BidSubmitter` + standby TAN lookup; `WizardPrep`.

   ```python
   async def _evaluate(browser_session: BrowserSession, js: str, *args):
       """...Not `must_get_current_page().evaluate`: that builds a new Page actor per call, which attaches a NEW CDP session... (reh_3d86cd104c8eb1b5)."""
       cdp = await browser_session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
       expression = f"({js.strip()})({', '.join(json.dumps(a) for a in args)})"
       result = await cdp.cdp_client.send.Runtime.evaluate(
           params={"expression": expression, "returnByValue": True, "awaitPromise": True}, session_id=cdp.session_id)
       if "exceptionDetails" in result:
           raise RuntimeError(f"JavaScript evaluation failed: {result['exceptionDetails']}")
       raw = result.get("result", {}).get("value")
       if isinstance(raw, (dict, list)):
           return raw
       raw = "" if raw is None else raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)   # as Page.evaluate returned it
       try:
           return json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw[:1] in ("[", "{") else raw
       except ValueError:
           return raw
   ```

   Lifecycle routing in `_enable_page_monitoring_routed` now feeds all of a target's queues:

   ```python
   routes = self.__dict__.setdefault("_lifecycle_routes", {})

   def route(event, session_id=None):
       target = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if session_id else None
       item = {"name": event.get("name", "unknown"), "loaderId": event.get("loaderId", "none"),
               "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()}
       for queue in routes.get(target, ()):
   ```

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import threading

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    """Ends the process itself (no shutdown of leftover tasks, see _exit_now)."""
    _exit_now(await run_once())


async def run_once() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    if token:
        _deadline_watchdog(task)
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    try:
        async with async_playwright() as playwright:
            answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    except Exception as error:
        logging.getLogger("agent").error("Workflow failed: %s", error)
        return 1
    if answer is None:
        print("Portal submission confirmed; no API answer to post"
              if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else "No answer to submit", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


def _exit_now(code: int) -> None:
    """Leave without waiting for leftover tasks, threads or browser connections: run reh_3d75a2747df66520 logged
    "Workflow failed" at 19:20 and then hung in shutdown until it was cancelled at 25:20."""
    logging.shutdown()
    sys.stdout.flush()
    sys.stderr.flush()
    os._exit(code)


def _deadline_watchdog(task: dict) -> None:
    """A thread that ends the process once the run has expired, whatever the event loop is doing."""
    left = contract.seconds_left(task)
    if left != float("inf"):
        timer = threading.Timer(max(left + 5, 1), lambda: (print("run expired: exiting", flush=True), _exit_now(1)))
        timer.daemon = True
        timer.start()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\crubs\.claude\skills\caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations reader can't decode. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl) — prose words only, never real code symbols/function names. Strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "每繪新生對象參照，故重繪；以 useMemo 包之則免。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Project guide: Atira EHL challenge agent ("From RFQ to bid")

A Python agent that, at run time, uses a model (hosted Qwen) to navigate four websites (tender portal, supplier portal,
ERP, webmail), work out the task from the brief, and submit one answer. Brief: `atira challenge rfq`.
Platform docs: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start and `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md`.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point. Write the agent in `solve(task, page)`. |
| `run.py` | Run contract: `load_run`, `submit_answer`, `seconds_left`. Platform plumbing, change rarely. |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers (CDP); locally starts Chromium. |
| `models.py` | `ask_qwen`, `ask_clef`, `qwen()` (OpenAI SDK client). |
| `agent.json` | Sandbox config: `setup`, `run`, `models` (hosted models to wait for), optional `"browsers": 1-4`. |
| `swarm/`, `agents/` | Agent-swarm framework and one file per agent: see `docs/SWARM.md` (read before adding an agent). |
| `tests/` | Unit tests against fakes. |

`task` has `brief`, `access` (site ids, URLs, credentials), `submission` (`api` or `site`) and `answer_schema`.
For `api` submissions return the answer from `solve()`; for `site` submissions enter it on the website and return `None`.

## Rules that decide whether a submission is accepted

- A model must pick navigation targets and make decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts, crawlers
  or copied values. A coding agent reviews every package. Helpers (parsing, pagination of a model-selected result set,
  validation, form filling) are fine.
- A scored run lasts 20 min. Submit the best answer about 1 min before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`); late = 0.
- Max 4 browsers, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. The sandbox only reaches the platform and the websites.
- Package: max 20 MB compressed, `agent.json` at the root. Never include `.env` or keys (they are git-ignored).
- Hosted models are free, but each call adds simulated cost to ranking (quality, then cost x time). Use Qwen for
  easy steps; first call after idle can take several minutes, so use long timeouts.

## Setup per laptop (once)

Prerequisites: Git, Python is NOT required (uv manages 3.12), and a GitHub account that is on the Atira team.

### Windows (PowerShell)
```powershell
irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # Atira CLI (read the script first if you prefer)
winget install --id astral-sh.uv -e                           # uv
# open a NEW terminal so PATH updates
atira login                                                   # browser sign-in with GitHub
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
```

### macOS / Linux
```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh     # Atira CLI; then add ~/.local/bin to PATH
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh               # uv (or: brew install uv)
# open a NEW terminal
atira login
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium        # on Linux add: uv run playwright install-deps chromium
```

### Both: Claude Code helpers (optional)
```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # lets Claude read run logs, model calls, timings, compare runs
```
Check with `atira whoami`. Use `atira login --device` if no browser is available.

## Develop locally

Two terminals, both in the repo root.

Terminal 1 (leave open): the free-model proxy.
```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2: load scouting env, then run the agent.
```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
```sh
# macOS / Linux
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
`atira scout --env` sets `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, site URLs and the `QWEN_*` / `CLEF_*`
variables pointing at the local proxy. The variables only live in that terminal. Local runs use the public
scouting logins: nothing done there is scored, and answers entered on the tender portal never count. Local model calls
are free and unranked. `atira scout` (no flag) prints the logins and brief for manual browsing.

Unit tests: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -q` (add pytest with `uv add --dev pytest` if missing).

## Test in the real sandbox

```sh
atira test-run . --follow        # same sandbox as scored runs, public dataset, up to 2 h, not ranked
atira test-run . --dry-run       # only shows what would be packed (no upload)
```
Max 3 test runs waiting at once. Inspect results:
```sh
atira status                     # latest submissions and test runs
atira logs <run-id> --follow     # reh_... (test run) or run_... (scored run)
atira package <id>               # what was uploaded
atira cancel <run-id>
```
With the `atira` MCP server Claude can also fetch logs by time, model calls, where time went, browser screens and
compare two runs. Ask it "why did run reh_xxx fail?".

## Run data: save it locally, read it locally first (rule for Claude Code)

The platform (atira CLI and `atira` MCP) is often slow (calls over 2 min) or unreachable, and it keeps only part of a
long log. So every piece of run data that gets pulled is also stored locally in `.swarm/runs/`, and that copy is read
first.

- **Full logs**: `scripts/pull-run.ps1 <run> [-Follow]` writes `.swarm/runs/<run>-log.md` (the whole log, replaced on
  each pull). A Monitor that follows a run also writes the whole stream into that file (`... | tee -a <file> | grep ...`),
  not only the filtered lines.
- **Everything else** (MCP `get_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`, `diagnose_run`, `compare_runs`, what a
  screenshot showed): right after pulling, append it to `.swarm/runs/<run>.md` as a section
  `## <UTC time> - <tool and arguments>` with the result (drop noise, keep scores, errors, timings, key lines).
- **Index**: `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`, one line per run: run id, date, what the package changed, outcome (quality, time,
  answer), main findings. Update it whenever a run is started, ends, or is analysed.
- **Read first**: before calling the platform, check `.swarm/runs/`; call it only for data that is missing there or
  outdated (a run still going). If the platform does not answer, work from the local files and say so.
- **Local runs** (scouting sites, `atira models proxy` running): `scripts/local-run.ps1 -Only "AgentA,AgentB" -Name x`
  runs headless and writes the whole log to `.swarm/local/<time>-<name>.md`. Use them (in the background) to check a
  fix before spending a sandbox test run; note the result in `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md` under "Local checks".
- `.swarm/` is git-ignored and not packaged (`atira test-run . --dry-run` lists it as ignored). The files hold scenario
  values: never copy anything from them into the package.

## Submit (ranked, public)

Run a test run first and make sure it finishes with a valid answer. Then agree in the team who submits
(one submission in flight per team, and it is public and final).
```sh
atira submit . --dry-run         # check the package
atira submit . --follow          # review -> one scored run on the public dataset -> leaderboard
atira leaderboard
```
The final ranking uses a private dataset with different websites and data, so build a general agent that does not
rely on public-dataset specifics. Choose the final attempt with `atira final [--best-of 1|3]` before the final run
starts (own model keys cost up to 3x).

## Models

- Default: hosted `qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, up to 32 concurrent calls/team) via `models.qwen()`; `clef` (image
  decision model, 16 concurrent) via `models.ask_clef`. List every hosted model used in `agent.json` `"models"`.
- Own provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, ...) are stored as team secrets on the team page and go through the run's
  metering proxy. See the run contract, section LLM calls.
- Claude Code (this assistant) is only for writing code and runs on your own Claude. Optional experimental launcher
  `claude-atira` (Windows, per-user setup, not in the repo) points Claude Code at Qwen; plain `claude` is the default.

## Team workflow

See `docs/COLLABORATION.md` (baseline, `scripts/team.py status|sync|integrate`, CI) and `docs/INTEGRATION.md`
(what came from which branch, open contract questions).

- Commit with normal `git commit` / `git push` so Entire checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` branches.
- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys. `.entire/settings.json` is shared; `settings.local.json` is personal.
- Pull before starting, keep commits small, and say in the team chat before running `atira submit`.

## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)

Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.

### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
| Site | Holds | Traps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)
- Quantity = tender qty, overridden by the latest clarification per position; withdrawn answers ignored.
- Requirement = spec revision marked *current*, with scoped amendments applied.
- Material = active ERP material matching bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification EXACTLY; none -> "no bid".
- Price = valid price condition on scenario date at highest reached quantity scale, minus approved discount, round half-up
  to the cent, converted to EUR. Discount = latest sales-director approval for this exact tender (conditional thresholds), else 0%.
- Lead time = stock if it covers qty, else production lead time; shared stock is all-or-nothing per material.
- Konditionsgruppen decide if discount hits base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup fees never discounted.
- Packaging cartons, shared setup/pool fees, delivery commitments allocated per position; project bonus = marginal
  percentage bands allocated proportionally in cents; final price formula rounds ONCE at the end.
- Metal-index rates selected by date; nominal stroke derived from reserves.
- Authority: only authorised senders + exact tender reference; newest valid record wins.
- Partial submission allowed (explicitly omitted positions) but bid must still be signed. Missing material -> no bid.

### Scoring / ranking
- Quality 0-100: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 (minus extra checks), total 5, arithmetic consistency 5;
  +5 each for withdrawn-quantity and metal-index checks when present. Per position: material 20%, quantity 15%,
  base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
- Correct tender reference is mandatory (else ineligible, ranked after all eligible).
- Order: eligible -> quality (higher) -> cost x time (lower; cost = simulated model prices, time = wall clock to accepted answer).
- Final ranking: PRIVATE dataset first, then public, then "system elegance". Private = same jobs/rules/format but different
  software, layouts, names, content, data. Do NOT tune to public-1; derive everything from the sites at runtime.
- Private run uses latest passing submission (or best of 3 if opted in via `atira final --best-of 3`).

### Fair play (an AI reviewer reads the whole package: passed / flagged / rejected)
Forbidden: any scenario value in the package (code, config, prompts, notes, defaults, fallbacks: prices, material numbers,
totals, discounts, tender refs, logins, TANs); pre-solving the answer (yourself or with an assistant) and shipping it;
fixed click paths; crawl-everything-then-one-model-call; model only as fallback; contacting hosts other than platform + 4 sites;
models outside the proxy; local/bundled models; starting own browsers (even headless; extras are killed); attacking platform/sites;
sharing scored-run data. Never write notes addressed to the reviewer (steering counts against us).
Allowed: any agent design, any provider via the proxy with team-secret keys, own code/prompts/tools, OSS libs installed in
`setup`, knowledge from scouting/test runs (as general strategy, never as values), helper code for browser control, parsing,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling, paging through results the model selected.
Helpers MAY NOT discover and traverse the sites to assemble evidence: the model decides where to go, what to search, what matters.

### Building an agent swarm
- Multiple agents/processes/threads are explicitly allowed; no limit on agent count, only **max 4 browsers** (`"browsers": n`
  in `agent.json`, CDP urls in `CDP_URLS`, browser n = display `:n`, CDP port 9221+n). Tabs/contexts inside them are unlimited.
- Frameworks: nothing is whitelisted or banned; any open-source library (respect licence) installed during `setup`
  (network allowed there, no credentials). Toolchains: Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24 (+pnpm, bun, runs .ts), Rust/cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq.
  Run phase is offline except platform + sites + model proxy. Package <= 20 MB. Plain asyncio/threads + OpenAI SDK is enough;
  agent frameworks (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, browser-use, etc.) are fine if they use the proxy base URLs
  and the provided CDP browsers (never launch their own Chromium in scored runs; connect via CDP).
- Suggested shape: an orchestrator (model) that reads the brief and spawns one worker per site / per position
  (tender, spec, ERP, mail run in parallel on separate browsers), workers return structured evidence with source + timestamps,
  a calculator step (plain code, deterministic rounding rules) computes prices, a verifier agent cross-checks authority/dates/
  tender reference/superseded records, then one agent fills the configurator and signs with the TAN.
- Models: hosted `qwen` (32 concurrent, 256k ctx, vision) for navigation/extraction; `clef` (16 concurrent) for quick
  choice/score decisions; use a stronger own-key model only for hard reasoning (cost x time only matters as tie-break after quality,
  so quality first). Every call counts simulated cost, so keep prompts short and use cached prefixes. Warm-up can take minutes: long timeouts.
  List hosted models in `agent.json` `"models"` (`[]` skips warm-up wait).
- All LLM traffic via `$LLM_PROXY_URL` / `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`; send your own User-Agent on platform HTTP calls (default Python UA gets 403).

### Run discipline
- Clock starts at the `run` command; scored 20 min; submit the best answer by ~1 min before end (`run.seconds_left`); late/no answer = 0.
- Build a fallback: keep a best-so-far answer and submit it on a timer even if the swarm is unfinished.
- Submission 400 with `issues` is not final (fix + resend); 202 is final and the process has 10 s to exit.
- Sessions time out (ERP, portals): handle re-login. Prefer partial-correct signed bid over nothing.
- Test runs (2 h, unscored) on public data first; use `atira` MCP (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`) to debug.
  Never copy values from logs/screenshots/answers into the package.

### Links
Challenge: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq · fair play: /docs/fair-play.md · run contract: /docs/run-contract.md ·
API: /docs/api.md · CLI: /docs/cli.md · llms.txt: /llms.txt · leaderboard: /challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md

# Notes for AI coding agents

- This repo is an Atira EHL challenge agent (starter kit). Python 3.12 + uv, Playwright, hosted Qwen via OpenAI SDK.
- Your agent goes in `solve(task, page)` in `agent.py`. `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` are platform plumbing.
- `agent.json` defines how the sandbox installs/runs (`uv sync`, `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`) and which hosted models it uses.
- A model must choose navigation/decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts or crawlers (submissions are reviewed).
- Scored run is 20 min: submit the best answer ~1 minute before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`).
- Local run: terminal 1 `atira models proxy`; terminal 2 `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression` then `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`.
- Test in the real sandbox: `atira test-run . --follow`. Ranked submit: `atira submit . --follow` (only when the team agrees).
- The `atira` MCP server is available for debugging runs (logs, model calls, timing).
- Only inspect, save, or reference run data for runs the user identifies as theirs or runs launched for them with a recorded launch receipt. Historical indexes and visible team runs are not proof of ownership. Never collect other teams' run data.
- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys.
- This repo uses Entire: commit your work with normal `git commit` / `git push` so session
  checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` shadow branches manually.

## Working alongside the rest of the team (read docs/COLLABORATION.md)

- `main` is the shared baseline; other developers and their agents work on other branches at the same time.
- **At the start of every task** run `uv run --no-sync python scripts/team.py status --json` and read
  `docs/INTEGRATION.md`. Do not build what already exists in `main` or on another branch; extend it.
- If your branch is behind `main`, run `uv run --no-sync python scripts/team.py sync` (safe: changes nothing unless the
  merge is clean and the tests pass) before editing files that `main` also changed.
- Before changing a file that `status` lists as changed on another branch, say so to the user: it is a likely conflict.
- When two parts must agree (bid rules, result shapes, number formats), extend `tests/test_contracts.py`.
- One task per worktree: `git worktree add ../<task> -b <user>/<task> origin/main`. Never edit another agent's worktree.
- Never commit `.integration/` or `.swarm/`; never force-push; never push to `main` (the integrator moves it).

- [No blocking waits](feedback-no-blocking-waits.md) — keep coding while test runs go; use Monitor, never long sleep loops
- [atira CLI path](atira-cli-path.md) — not on Git Bash PATH; use full atira.cmd path in Bash/Monitor
- [Swarm run findings](swarm-run-findings.md) — 2026-10-10 runs: ERP step exhaustion, strict matcher, early COLLECT exit, mail dupes, log truncation
- [Local run logs](feedback-local-run-logs.md) — save every pulled run log/MCP result as .md in .swarm/runs/, read those first
- [Commit via PowerShell](commit-via-powershell.md) — Entire's commit hook hangs under Git Bash; commit from PowerShell, check the trailer

## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)

Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.

### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
| Site | Holds | Traps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)
- Quantity = tender qty, overridden by the latest clarification per position; withdrawn answers ignored.
- Requirement = spec revision marked *current*, with scoped amendments applied.
- Material = active ERP material matching bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification EXACTLY; none -> "no bid".
- Price = valid price condition on scenario date at highest reached quantity scale, minus approved discount, round half-up
  to the cent, converted to EUR. Discount = latest sales-director approval for this exact tender (conditional thresholds), else 0%.
- Lead time = stock if it covers qty, else production lead time; shared stock is all-or-nothing per material.
- Konditionsgruppen decide if discount hits base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup fees never discounted.
- Packaging cartons, shared setup/pool fees, delivery commitments allocated per position; project bonus = marginal
  percentage bands allocated proportionally in cents; final price formula rounds ONCE at the end.
- Metal-index rates selected by date; nominal stroke derived from reserves.
- Authority: only authorised senders + exact tender reference; newest valid record wins.
- Partial submission allowed (explicitly omitted positions) but bid must still be signed. Missing material -> no bid.

### Scoring / ranking
- Quality 0-100: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 (minus extra checks), total 5, arithmetic consistency 5;
  +5 each for withdrawn-quantity and metal-index checks when present. Per position: material 20%, quantity 15%,
  base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
- Correct tender reference is mandatory (else ineligible, ranked after all eligible).
- Order: eligible -> quality (higher) -> cost x time (lower; cost = simulated model prices, time = wall clock to accepted answer).
- Final ranking: PRIVATE dataset first, then public, then "system elegance". Private = same jobs/rules/format but different
  software, layouts, names, content, data. Do NOT tune to public-1; derive everything from the sites at runtime.
- Private run uses latest passing submission (or best of 3 if opted in via `atira final --best-of 3`).

### Fair play (an AI reviewer reads the whole package: passed / flagged / rejected)
Forbidden: any scenario value in the package (code, config, prompts, notes, defaults, fallbacks: prices, material numbers,
totals, discounts, tender refs, logins, TANs); pre-solving the answer (yourself or with an assistant) and shipping it;
fixed click paths; crawl-everything-then-one-model-call; model only as fallback; contacting hosts other than platform + 4 sites;
models outside the proxy; local/bundled models; starting own browsers (even headless; extras are killed); attacking platform/sites;
sharing scored-run data. Never write notes addressed to the reviewer (steering counts against us).
Allowed: any agent design, any provider via the proxy with team-secret keys, own code/prompts/tools, OSS libs installed in
`setup`, knowledge from scouting/test runs (as general strategy, never as values), helper code for browser control, parsing,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling, paging through results the model selected.
Helpers MAY NOT discover and traverse the sites to assemble evidence: the model decides where to go, what to search, what matters.

### Building an agent swarm
- Multiple agents/processes/threads are explicitly allowed; no limit on agent count, only **max 4 browsers** (`"browsers": n`
  in `agent.json`, CDP urls in `CDP_URLS`, browser n = display `:n`, CDP port 9221+n). Tabs/contexts inside them are unlimited.
- Frameworks: nothing is whitelisted or banned; any open-source library (respect licence) installed during `setup`
  (network allowed there, no credentials). Toolchains: Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24 (+pnpm, bun, runs .ts), Rust/cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq.
  Run phase is offline except platform + sites + model proxy. Package <= 20 MB. Plain asyncio/threads + OpenAI SDK is enough;
  agent frameworks (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, browser-use, etc.) are fine if they use the proxy base URLs
  and the provided CDP browsers (never launch their own Chromium in scored runs; connect via CDP).
- Suggested shape: an orchestrator (model) that reads the brief and spawns one worker per site / per position
  (tender, spec, ERP, mail run in parallel on separate browsers), workers return structured evidence with source + timestamps,
  a calculator step (plain code, deterministic rounding rules) computes prices, a verifier agent cross-checks authority/dates/
  tender reference/superseded records, then one agent fills the configurator and signs with the TAN.
- Models: hosted `qwen` (32 concurrent, 256k ctx, vision) for navigation/extraction; `clef` (16 concurrent) for quick
  choice/score decisions; use a stronger own-key model only for hard reasoning (cost x time only matters as tie-break after quality,
  so quality first). Every call counts simulated cost, so keep prompts short and use cached prefixes. Warm-up can take minutes: long timeouts.
  List hosted models in `agent.json` `"models"` (`[]` skips warm-up wait).
- All LLM traffic via `$LLM_PROXY_URL` / `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`; send your own User-Agent on platform HTTP calls (default Python UA gets 403).

### Run discipline
- Clock starts at the `run` command; scored 20 min; submit the best answer by ~1 min before end (`run.seconds_left`); late/no answer = 0.
- Build a fallback: keep a best-so-far answer and submit it on a timer even if the swarm is unfinished.
- Submission 400 with `issues` is not final (fix + resend); 202 is final and the process has 10 s to exit.
- Sessions time out (ERP, portals): handle re-login. Prefer partial-correct signed bid over nothing.
- Test runs (2 h, unscored) on public data first; use `atira` MCP (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`) to debug.
  Never copy values from logs/screenshots/answers into the package.

- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.
